chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no harm in the leftover of the cat: wudu (ablution) may be performed from it and it may be drunk. And the leftover of the dog is not to be drunk, unless it is a large basin from which water is drawn.

key_terms.حَوْضًا كَبِيرًا: a large basin or large body of collected water
key_terms.سُؤْرُ الْكَلْبِ: the leftover water from which a dog has drunk
key_terms.فَضْلِ السِّنَّوْرِ: the leftover water or remainder associated with a cat
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأَ: to perform wudu (ablution) with that water
key_terms.يُسْتَسْقَى مِنْهُ: water is drawn or taken from it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use or drink water left over by a cat or a dog in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the purity and use of water left over by animals. It states that the leftover of a cat is permissible for wudu (ablution) and drinking, while the leftover of a dog is not to be drunk, except where it is part of a large body of water from which water is drawn.
